correctness.rationale: For n>=5 with strictly positive vertex-specific one-way rates, the RK4 polynomial has no wrapped walks of <=4 jumps. Exact path expansion using complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials yields five entry types by forward distance. Distance 0,2,4 stay strictly positive (Taylor remainder/discriminant), while distance-one entry is hr_iF_{r_i,r_{i+1}}(h) and distance-three is h³Πr(4-hΣ_4r)/24. The negative discriminant for F' makes F strictly decreasing with one root and proves a single sharp intersection cutoff. Independently computed exact rational RK4 matrix powers for three heterogeneous/homogeneous n=5,6,7 examples and checked every entry against the symbolic formulas, all row sums one. Symbolically checked F(2/(a+b))=1/3 and the single-defect cubic substitution; these support the analytic no-reentry proof. The four-maximum plateau criterion follows because each one-jump root is >1/M and 4/W is =1/M iff W=4M. Diagonal <=1 in a nonnegative stochastic matrix gives Mh*<α, while the single-high-rate defect yields sharp supremum α; the changeover R_c is the unique root >1 of 3R³-9R²-15R-43. No correctness defect found.

value.rationale: Unmodified RK4 on finite nonreversible Markov cycles is a natural numerical diffusion problem. An exact timestep law valid for arbitrary heterogeneous rates, using only adjacent pairs and four consecutive rates rather than a full matrix positivity test, directly characterizes a meaningful CFL frontier. The exact plateau criterion explains when RK4 genuinely outperforms forward Euler; the sharp universal gain and one-defect phase switch reveal nontrivial structure. These are motivated complete family-level invariants, not arbitrary isolated calculations.

limitations: Only n>=5 strictly positive one-way cyclic rates and classical RK4 completed endpoints; no internal stage positivity.
The sharp ratio α is a strict supremum approached by unbounded single-rate contrast, never attained.
